title: Anastasia Labs - Streamlining Development: A User-Friendly Smart Contract Library for Plutarch and Aiken Design Patterns & Efficiency

ms.promise: Robust documentation of unintuitive / hacky design patterns published to a standalone Github repository, as-well-as to existing developer documentation Github repositories such as the Plutonomicon, Developer Portal, Aiken Documentation, and Plutarch Documentation.
ms.criteria:
Following design patterns are clearly written and published in Anastasia Labs Github repository
・Transaction level validation for spending validators via stake validators using the withdraw zero trick.
・Transaction level validation for spending validators via minting policies.
・Input/output indexing with redeemers.
・Strict && validation checks
・PlutusTypeEnum Redeemers - efficient data encoding for simple redeemers as Enums.
・Normalize txInfoMint to get rid of 0 lovelace value.
・Normalize Validity Range.
ms.report:
We have the following design patterns clearly written and published in Anastasia Labs Github repository
・Transaction level validation for spending validators via stake validators using the withdraw zero trick.
・Transaction level validation for spending validators via minting policies.
・Input/output indexing with redeemers.
・Strict && validation checks
・PlutusTypeEnum Redeemers - efficient data encoding for simple redeemers as Enums.
・Normalize txInfoMint to get rid of 0 lovelace value.
・Normalize Validity Range.

All documentation for the design patter can be found at: https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/design-patterns

ms.promise: A series of unit-tests and property based tests that provide some assurance that the implementations of the wrapper functions adhere to their technical specifications.
ms.criteria:

・Property-Based Testing Success: The acceptance criteria for property-based testing will involve demonstrating that the properties and invariants specified for the wrapper libraries are satisfied across a wide range of generated test cases.
・Test Documentation Completeness: The documentation for unit tests and property-based tests should be complete, including clear descriptions of the tests, their pur
ms.report:
Happy to submit PoA for milestone 4!
The PoA contains:
1) Tests and how to run them:
These are published on Anastasia Labs' GitHub repository, along with clear instructions on how to run the tests both in our report showcasing our testing suite and our individual repositories README.md sections:
In our "Testing Suite" report: Aiken (Page 2), Plutarch (Page 54)
Aiken GitHub repository: https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/aiken-design-patterns/blob/main/README.md
Plutarch GitHub repository: https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/plutarch-design-patterns/blob/main/README.md
2) Test Results Evidence
Our successful test runs can be observed via a terminal run we have prepared as a GIF, showcases all our tests passing. Alternatively our GitHub actions section of each commit we have pushed to these repositories as they are part of our Github CI Workflow display the tests are running:
GIF Testrun - Aiken: https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/aiken-design-patterns/blob/main/assets/images/aiken-design-patterns.gif
GIF Testrun - Plutarch: https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/plutarch-design-patterns/blob/test/property-based-tests/assets/images/plutarch-design-patterns.gif
More evidence can be gathered by following the guidelines to setup your developer environment found in each of the repositories README and run the tests yourself to see the result.
3) Documentation
We have prepared an extensive testing suite and this needed to be documented well so patterns can be understood better. To individually understand what is happening in each test it would be advisable to refer to the main repository: https://github.com/Anastasia-Labs/design-patterns. We explain each concept from a high level overview for better understanding of these patterns
Link to documentation PDF: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Oju4cMF7jrIjh5VbIueTyp45T45g1159/view?usp=sharing
